question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

events.title: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
events.description:

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched control over the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced through sustained anti-corruption campaigns and personnel purges in the military and central bodies, underpins the overwhelming trader consensus against his departure before 2027. At age 73, he shows no public signals of stepping aside, and analysts widely expect him to secure a fourth term as general secretary at the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027, with loyalists positioned to fill reshuffled Politburo and Central Committee roles under informal age norms. No designated successor has emerged, and elite networks remain aligned with his priorities on stability and discipline. While health developments, unforeseen elite realignments, or major external shocks could theoretically alter the timeline, current indicators point to continuity through the congress and beyond.
